diagnostics.message: Heading marker has no title: 第一章 (PDF page 7).
Printed contents has 2 unreadable rows; inferred hierarchy may omit parents or children.

blind_protocol: Runtime hashes frozen before selecting Beijing chemistry and Renjiao geography; printed contents visually labelled and PDF offsets checked before recognition; no algorithm changes after results. v0.4.0 chemistry and Guangdong geography are now regression samples, with original results preserved.

failure_analysis.finding: All four unmatched printed titles have the correct destination page and depth but OCR glyph substitutions. No title repair using reference labels or book-specific spelling rules was added; use the reviewed manual TOC fallback.
100-DPI grayscale JPEG-quality-30 derivative remains 16/32 strict reference matches; this is a stress test, not a new independent book.

Several older books only label chapters/numbered sections. Their extra candidates remain unlabelled; full-output precision claims apply only to complete-contents samples. Diagnostics are evidence conflicts, not calibrated confidence.

maintenance_comparison.metric_policy: Complete printed contents; strict normalized title/PDF page/depth, all output candidates including extras and duplicates. Outside-contents headings can still be valid navigation.

performance.method: Linux fresh Python processes, four OCR workers, 200 DPI, pinned same models/dependencies, warm filesystem. A-B then B-A per book after other benchmarks finished. Extraction includes native analysis, OCR and layout extraction; outline is title filtering/alignment/tree. A separate single-page OCR probe includes rendering/OCR/layout and records its output hash. Memory uses kernel resource.getrusage ru_maxrss: parent peak and largest waited child peak, separately, not simultaneous total process-tree memory. Linux KiB converted to MiB. No write/verification is timed here. Initial /proc memory experiment was discarded because the sandbox uses PID namespaces; only these kernel-based reruns are reported.
performance.driver:
"""Isolated before/after profile; source is embedded in the published evidence."""
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

if __name__ == '__main__':
    script_dir, source = sys.argv[1:3]
    sys.path.insert(0, script_dir)
    import add_bookmarks as app
    start = time.perf_counter()
    pages, scanned, visual = app.read_pages(source, lang='chi_sim+eng', workers=4, dpi=200)
    extraction = time.perf_counter() - start
    start = time.perf_counter()
    headings = app.headings_from_pages(pages, scanned, pdf_type='textbook', visual=visual)
    tree = app.build_tree_from_headings(headings)
    outline_seconds = time.perf_counter()-start
    probe_page = 7 if 'chemistry' in source else 15
    start = time.perf_counter()
    result = app._read_image_page((source, probe_page-1, 'chi_sim+eng', app.find_tesseract(), False, 200))
    import hashlib
    import resource
    print(json.dumps(dict(version=app.VERSION, pages=len(pages), ocr_pages=len(scanned), bookmarks=len(tree), extraction_seconds=extraction, outline_seconds=outline_seconds, ocr_probe_pdf_page=probe_page, ocr_probe_seconds=time.perf_counter()-start, ocr_probe_sha256=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(result,ensure_ascii=False).encode()).hexdigest(), parent_peak_rss_mib=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss/1024, largest_child_peak_rss_mib=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss/1024)))
performance.reproduction: Extract baseline scripts from Git commit 1217693; run the embedded driver with arguments <script-directory> <unbookmarked-input.pdf> in fresh Python processes. For each of the two pinned regression books use baseline/current then current/baseline, four workers and 200 DPI. Run without concurrent benchmark jobs. Linux ru_maxrss measures separate per-process peaks, not aggregate simultaneous memory.

maintenance_comparison.ci_policy: Retain all 12 OS/Python combinations and OCR-required tests. Prior CI timings are a single historical run, not a controlled performance baseline; no CI optimization is claimed.
